Method of Attack: Botnet malware infecting IoT devices, modems, and routers
DDoS attacks including DNS amplification, TCP/UDP floods, HTTP floods, SSL/TLS attacks
SSH/Telnet brute-forcing and exploits for spreading
Hijacking computational resources for crypto-mining and DDoS
String obfuscation and C2 server hidden behind Tor nodes
Impacted Systems: Routers including Seowon Intech SLC-130 and SLR-120S, D-Link DWR, iRZ mobile routers, TOTOLINK routers, Apache HTTP servers, ThinkPHP CMS, Zyxel P660HN routers, NETGEAR routers, Zhone routers
Attack Vector: Exploitation of multiple remote code execution and arbitrary code injection vulnerabilities (e.g., CVE-2020-17456, CVE-2018-10823, CVE-2022-27226, CVE-2022-25075 to 25084, CVE-2021-44228, CVE-2021-41773, CVE-2018-20062, CVE-2017-18368, CVE-2016-6277, CVE-2015-2051, CVE-2014-9118, NETGEAR DGN1000 exploit)
Use of hardcoded and updateable download servers for payload delivery
Indicators of Compromise: C2 server hidden behind Tor nodes
Commands such as ADNS, ARK, BLACKNURSE, DNS, HOLD, HTTP, JUNK, OVH, STD, TCP, TLS, UDP, OVERTCP, STOP, LDSERVER, SCANNER, SH, TCPOFF, TCPON
Use of multiple architecture-specific binaries (x86, x64, i686, darwin, bsd, arm, arm64, ppc, m68k, spc)
